Kim / team,

Draft language below — high level approach and then suggested contract text you can drop into the exhibit. Happy to refine with Laura on the call Wednesday.

Approach: keep inspection scope narrow and operationally predictable. Two levers: (1) time-boxed pen-test windows (staging only unless otherwise agreed), and (2) evidence cadence that separates automated operational artifacts (snapshots/logs) from formal attestation (SOC 2 report). 

Suggested exhibit snippets (place into Security Exhibit):
1) Penetration Testing. Customer may perform mutually scheduled penetration testing against Redwood staging environments during a 5-business-day window per request, provided Customer gives Redwood no less than 10 business days advance notice. Production testing is prohibited unless expressly authorized in writing by Redwood and subject to a separate control-plan and additional fees.

2) Forensic/Inspection Access. Redwood will provide read-only, short-lived access tokens or a jump-box to Customer for log review and forensic analysis during the agreed inspection window. Access will be scoped to agreed systems and will not include elevated administrative credentials. Any data extraction will be limited to logs and artifacts reasonably necessary for the investigation.

3) Evidence & SOC 2. Redwood will provide automated weekly operational snapshots (logs, relevant configuration) for the duration of the engagement upon request and will supply an ISO-formatted monthly attestation summary that maps to SOC 2 categories (availability, security). Full SOC 2 reports will be provided under NDA as standard practice following Redwood's reporting cadence.

Fallback / Remediation: If testing identifies a critical vulnerability, Redwood will prioritize a remediation plan and provide a remediation SLO: initial triage within 48 hours and a fix-or-mitigation plan within 10 business days.

Notes for Sales: avoid language that implies unlimited inspection rights or on-demand production access. Laura: if you see any redline that creates an open-ended "right to inspect" or broad data export clause, push-back to a scoped extraction definition.

I'll prepare a redline of the exhibit and attach an editable version before the call.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
